title: Risk assessment for ART-20260905-004: Client filter defaults

risks.description: 'Stakeholder' is built on a candidate the requester did not mean. Four computable candidates and one non-computable one (OQ1) give different sets; the requester's recorded counter-example (a client sponsor has no allocation) does not separate them because client-role seats are governed by clientScopeId, not by any of the candidates. Building before the answer produces a filter that disagrees with what the product owner expects and cannot be corrected without re-reading every criterion marked conditional.
risks.mitigation: Gate 1 answers OQ1 with one example person for whom the candidates differ. No scenario is written for a conditional criterion until then (AC2, AC5, AC14-AC16).

risks.description: A second, softer definition of 'who is on a project' is added beside the one the read gate already enforces. Since 2026-08-24 redactForReader narrows every non-exempt internal seat to live ProjectMember projects; if the filter computes stakeholders from Allocation or Engagement names, a person can be a member with no allocation (project in the payload, absent from All) or allocated with no membership (option offered, payload withholds the records, the filter points at nothing).
risks.mitigation: BR1 requires one pure function; ADR ART-20260905-006 proposes that if the definition is ProjectMember the function is memberProjectIdsFor itself, and that any other definition is stated with the divergence from the read gate accepted in writing.

risks.description: The word 'None' is reused as the value. The Discipline facet already uses 'None' to mean 'records with no discipline yet', a real filter that returns rows (lib/tree.ts:389-394). A shared token in adjacent controls of the same bar means one of them is wrong in matchesFilters, in parseSavedFilters, or in the Filters chip count.
risks.mitigation: BR7: a typed sentinel on FilterState with an instructing caption ('Client: choose...'); every consumer that compares to the literal 'All' is moved to compare to the resting value.

risks.description: Existing reset paths hide everything. revealIssue (IssueWorkspace.tsx:992) and Clear (FilterBar.tsx:286) both reset to EMPTY_FILTERS; a saved view captured at the new resting state applies an empty grid; a pre-existing saved view with client 'All' silently changes meaning. These are regressions in behaviour people already rely on if the specification leaves them undefined.
risks.mitigation: OQ8 fixes the target of each reset and the treatment of the sentinel in saved views before planning; AC9, AC10 and AC12 carry the behaviour once fixed; scenarios pin each path.

risks.description: Per-person persistence lands on protected paths. If OQ5 is per person, a new reducer arm (lib/workspace.ts), an ACTION_PERMISSIONS row (lib/access.ts) and a change to EMPTY_FILTERS (lib/types.ts) are needed; if it is made a saved view, it reverses the 2026-08-31 saved-views decision that personal views are a non-goal.
risks.mitigation: Gate 3 with the architect for the plan; the ADR proposes the notificationPrefs shape (self-service gate, audited, no migration) and rejects the saved-view route; browser-local storage is recorded as the cheaper alternative if the owner reads 'for them' as per browser.

risks.description: A name-only join is reintroduced. Engagement.engagementLeader, projectManager and clientSponsor are free-text names with no personId; using them for stakeholder resolution either joins on display name (the seam the identity migration closed for new paths, CLAUDE.md) or forces a Prisma migration to ids on Engagement.
risks.mitigation: Conditional on OQ1 choosing (b). If chosen, the ADR is superseded by one that carries the schema change, and AC16 is kept to make the cost visible.

risks.description: Allocation is read as an access fact. The resource model keeps Allocation (capacity) and ProjectMember (access) as siblings answering different questions; a filter default computed from live allocations also needs a 'live' date rule the code does not define for this purpose and must take 'today' as a parameter to keep the computation pure.
risks.mitigation: Conditional on OQ1 choosing (a). BR10 keeps the read one-way; AC14 pins the date boundaries; 'today' is a parameter, never the clock.

risks.description: Reports misstate their scope. scopeLabel prints 'All clients - <org>' when client is 'All'; over a person-scoped view a Daily IMS or client pack would claim firm-wide coverage it does not have, the misread the scopeLabel comment already warns about.
risks.mitigation: AC13 and OQ9: the label states the actual scope and openClientPack refuses the resting state; the owner decides whether position figures count the whole workspace or the person's projects.

risks.description: The ProjectMember backfill may not have been committed against production. docs/verification-checklist.md has no entry for scripts/backfill-project-members.ts --commit. If OQ1 lands on ProjectMember and the backfill was not run, non-exempt internal seats already see an empty tree, and the request would be masking a live defect rather than describing a feature gap.
risks.mitigation: OQ12: confirm and record the backfill run before Gate 1 closes; if unrecorded, run the integrity audit and treat an empty tree for a staffed person as an incident, not as this feature.

risks.description: Accountable roles see nothing. An Engagement Leader (all 38 permissions per G7) or a Platform Administrator who holds no allocation and no membership would, under deny-by-default (BR2), see an empty All; the membership design already names the engagement leader as its known limitation. If the requester is ROLE_ADMIN, the whole-firm view they see today is the deliberate exemption, and narrowing the filter for exempt seats is a product choice the request does not state.
risks.mitigation: OQ7 and OQ11 answered at Gate 1; AC17 keeps isExempt and redactForReader unmodified either way.

reasons: The requester's own open question (what 'stakeholder' resolves to) is unanswered and blocks five criteria; the analysts were told to surface it, not pick, and none of the three did. The requirement analyst describes four candidates and adds ProjectMember (post-dates D1); the architecture analyst finds 'role scoped to the project' collapses into ProjectMember and that the client-sponsor example is handled by clientScopeId rather than by any candidate; the UX analyst adds 'named on the SOW' from A4 and notes Sow carries no person reference. All three agree the candidates yield different sets. Product owner decides.

Disagreement on whether part (2) is already built. The architecture and UX analysts read the 2026-08-24 project read gate (redactForReader, projectView, memberProjectIdsFor) as already delivering 'All shows only my projects' for every non-exempt internal seat, leaving only ROLE_ADMIN, the machine actor and records with no project ancestor as the visible change. The requirement analyst wrote the criteria as if the behaviour were new. The specification records both: AC2 verifies agreement with the read gate under ProjectMember and AC17 isolates the exempt-seat decision. Whether the requester holds ROLE_ADMIN (OQ11) settles which reading describes what they see.

Disagreement on persistence scope. The requirement analyst reads 'persists for them' as per person across devices (E3). The UX analyst recommends the per-person notificationPrefs shape (directory id, self-or-admin, audited) and rejects saved views and localStorage. The architecture analyst lists browser-local (P1), model preference (P2) and personal saved views (P3) with costs and does not choose, noting P1 touches no protected path. ADR ART-20260905-006 proposes P2 with P1 as the alternative the architect may prefer; OQ5 carries it to the product owner.

Disagreement on the token. The requester said 'None'; all three analysts reject reusing the string because the Discipline facet already uses 'None' as a real filter. The UX analyst wants an instructing caption; the architecture analyst asks whether 'None' is a filter value (storable in saved views) or a UI resting state. The specification requires a typed sentinel (BR7) and leaves the caption and the saved-view treatment to OQ8.

Disagreement on the client-sponsor example. The requester offered it as the case that separates the candidates. The architecture analyst finds it does not: a client-role sponsor is governed by clientScopeId and clientView, and an internal sponsor is a ProjectMember with PROJROLE_SPONSOR. The requirement analyst kept it as the requester's own words. The specification records both readings in OQ1 and asks for a different discriminating example.

Priority is a placeholder. The requester stated none; the schema requires one; P2 was entered from the canonical band definition and is flagged as E3 in OQ13 for the product owner to confirm or change.

Protected paths are implicated (lib/types.ts certainly; lib/workspace.ts and lib/access.ts if per-person persistence; prisma/schema.prisma only if Engagement names are chosen), so the plan will need Gate 3 with the architect regardless of which options are chosen.
